key_insight: The paper shows that in stochastic 2D vortex dynamics, choosing circulation preservation (SALT) versus energy preservation (SFLT) fundamentally changes how uncertainty is distributed across flow scales and space.
engineering_relevance: For turbulence modeling and uncertainty quantification, the invariant you preserve determines whether stochastic effects concentrate near sharp gradients or spread more diffusely through the domain.
method: Compared two geometric stochastic Euler frameworks: SALT and SFLT.
Analyzed how noise scales with wavenumber, finding SALT is more sensitive to high-frequency modes.
Tested both approaches on a traveling dipole, vortex merger, and forced-damped turbulence.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments reported in the abstract show SALT localizes variance near active vorticity gradients, while SFLT produces a broader variance field across the domain.
watch_item: The models appear to force a tradeoff between structure preservation and kinetic-energy preservation, so the choice of formulation must match the intended physical objective.
paper_title: Numerical comparison of energy- versus circulation-preserving stochastic vortex dynamics
